nodes.description: Address holding administrative privileges; can queue, cancel and execute timelocked transactions.
Address proposed as the next admin; must call acceptAdmin to take over the role.
Secondary role allowed to queue transactions alongside admin.
Minimum timelock delay that queued transactions must satisfy.
Flag enabling a one-time bootstrap of pendingAdmin by admin.
Mapping from transaction hash to queued/executed boolean state.
Constant 14 day window after eta during which a queued transaction may still execute.
Constant 24 hour lower bound enforced on delay.
Constant 30 day upper bound enforced on delay.
Initializes admin, operator, delay and admin_initialized after validating delay bounds.
Payable fallback that accepts plain ETH transfers.
Self-call only setter for the delay state variable.
Self-call only setter for the operator role.
Lets pendingAdmin become admin and clears pendingAdmin.
Sets pendingAdmin; self-call after initialization, admin-only for the first call.
Admin/operator only entry that hashes a pending call and marks it queued after checking eta against delay.
Admin only entry that clears the queued flag of a transaction hash.
Admin only entry that validates the timelock window and performs an arbitrary external call with value.
Internal view helper returning block.timestamp.
Caller-controlled address used for every authorization check and for admin assignment.
Miner-influenceable timestamp driving all timelock window checks.
Low-level target.call{value: value}(callData) forwarding arbitrary calldata and ETH to an admin-supplied address.

edges.reason: Constructor parameter admin_ is written into the admin state variable.
Constructor parameter delay_ initializes the delay state variable.
Constructor validates delay_ against MINIMUM_DELAY.
Constructor validates delay_ against MAXIMUM_DELAY.
setDelay writes the delay_ parameter into delay.
setDelay requires delay_ to be at least MINIMUM_DELAY.
setDelay requires delay_ to be at most MAXIMUM_DELAY.
setDelay authorization depends on msg.sender == address(this).
setOperator authorization depends on msg.sender == address(this).
setOperator writes the operator_ parameter into operator.
acceptAdmin requires msg.sender == pendingAdmin.
acceptAdmin assigns the caller to the admin state variable.
acceptAdmin copies the untrusted msg.sender into admin.
acceptAdmin resets pendingAdmin to address(0).
setPendingAdmin authorization depends on msg.sender and admin_initialized.
First setPendingAdmin call flips admin_initialized to true.
setPendingAdmin writes pendingAdmin_ into pendingAdmin.
queueTransaction requires msg.sender == admin or operator.
queueTransaction compares eta against block.timestamp obtained through getBlockTimestamp.
queueTransaction calls getBlockTimestamp to read the current time.
queueTransaction computes getBlockTimestamp().add(delay) with SafeMath addition.
queueTransaction hashes target into the txHash local.
queueTransaction hashes eta into the txHash local.
queueTransaction sets queuedTransactions[txHash] = true.
cancelTransaction requires msg.sender == admin.
cancelTransaction hashes target into the txHash local.
cancelTransaction hashes eta into the txHash local.
cancelTransaction sets queuedTransactions[txHash] = false.
executeTransaction requires msg.sender == admin.
executeTransaction enforces the timelock and grace window using block.timestamp.
executeTransaction calls getBlockTimestamp three times for its time checks.
executeTransaction hashes target into the txHash local.
executeTransaction hashes eta into the txHash local.
executeTransaction reads and then clears queuedTransactions[txHash].
executeTransaction computes eta.add(GRACE_PERIOD) with SafeMath addition.
executeTransaction derives the 4-byte selector from signature and packs it into callData.
executeTransaction appends data into callData.
Admin-supplied target becomes the receiver of the external low-level call.
Admin-supplied value is forwarded as ETH in the low-level call.
callData is the payload passed to the low-level call.
executeTransaction triggers the arbitrary low-level call before returning.
The arbitrary external call can re-enter the Timelock contract.
The low-level call returns the success flag checked by require.
The low-level call returns returnData which is propagated to the caller.
